summary.prose: S001 now renders a full 1MiB note in75-79ms on both native reference hosts, but its serial fidelity path still misses the1s acknowledgement target. This revision overlaps independent read-only checks after the unchanged300ms gap and adopts only fully checked immutable candidate proofs on exact canonical confirmation. Native application still requires current configured-codec authorization, independent host success and a final native version/digest match; all prior one-pane, recovery and action behavior remains. Performance is unqualified until the original native gate passes.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The daemon-owned private repository-keyed index remains authoritative for link resolution, backlinks and the title/preview list read-model. Client-side scratchpad editing now uses Milkdown + Crepe inside a VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider on the existing .md TextDocument, replacing the host's built-in vscode.markdown.editor. Insrc owns its selection toolbar and lock state without a native-editor extension API dependency. [[c40]] [[c41]] [[c42]]

ownedContracts.name: ScratchpadRef
ownedContracts.purpose: The one cross-cutting note-identity primitive every link-, lifecycle-, and citation-facing story needs: a stable reference to a scratchpad that survives rename/move/archive/restore. Owned at s1 (the Epic's root) because s2 — which depends only on s1, not on s7 where identity is semantically 'about' — also needs it for the k2 tie-break.

boundary.internal: Milkdown + Crepe hosted in one VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider pane is private to s1. It owns rendering/editing, per-pane lock/pencil controls, explicit selection Send popup, versioned transaction/document synchronization, local asset packaging and TextDocument lifecycle integration. It preserves the .md file and sc1 identity, replaces the old textarea/save protocol atomically and retains browse/new/delete/send/list-refresh behavior. Locked mode keeps selection and Send available; a custom tooltip may be needed because default formatting toolbars can hide when read-only. No s8 attachments, s7 metadata persistence, backlinks or search ranking are implemented here.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The chat-menu cap-10 rendering, the list panel's cap-20/3-line-preview/delete UI, and the relevance-ranking algorithm itself (title-first, tie-break via sc1's stableId) are private to s2; sc3 exposes only the read-model shape (title/preview/mtime), not the ranking logic.

Find-in-note's match highlighting, wraparound navigation, and collapsed-section reveal operate entirely on the open editor's live text buffer — no cross-story data or contract is produced or consumed.

The entry-boundary/timestamp Markdown convention, day-grouping, and the Undated bucket are private to how one note's content renders; no story downstream of s4 in the Epic's dependency graph consumes dated-entry structure, so it is not exposed as a shared contract.

The link-target picker UI and the qualified-target Markdown syntax (percent-encoded target segments, versioned, per the HLD's resolved open question) are private to s5; sc2 exposes only the resolved-reference and backlink-query shape s6 consumes, not the authoring UI or syntax.
The backlink view's grouping-by-source-note rendering, on the pad and on file/symbol surfaces, is private UI; no story is downstream of s6 in the Epic's graph, so it exposes no further contract.

The archive/restore state machine, the permanent-delete confirmation flow, and the decision of where stable ID/repo-association/archive-state are actually persisted are private to s7; it extends sc1's bare ScratchpadRef with lifecycle state but does not re-expose that lifecycle representation as a further contract, since s8/s9/s10 only need sc1's identity.

The attach-to-turn picker UI, the removable-preview rendering, and revision-pinning for a queued turn are private to s8; it consumes sc1 to cite the note and exposes no further contract, since only s9 depends on s8 and s9's own need (provenance link) is satisfied by sc1 directly.
The promote-to-draft action's brainstorm/ISSUE routing and idempotent-retry handling are private to s9; no story is downstream of s9 in the Epic's graph.
The tag-filter UI and starter-template catalog are private to s10; it extends sc3's list read-model with the tags field but no story is downstream of s10 in the Epic's graph.

nonFunctional.performance: The list panel (s2) must not re-parse every on-disk pad file per render; sc3's read-model is served from the daemon's index instead. Backlink-query latency targets and the note-size cap for sc2's new daemon IPC are explicitly an open PRD decision (DEF §8) to resolve before s2/s5/s6 build. Avoid full reparses/echo loops on selection updates; set a supported note-size/performance budget in S001 LLD.
nonFunctional.security: The home-dir scratchpad store stays outside repo enrollment per k4; the daemon's new index only joins validated target identity (sc1/sc2), never widening default document search or repo registration to the store itself. Bundle editor assets locally under CSP. Validate bridge actions, target URI and version; no arbitrary file paths, command dispatch or cloud calls from document content. Library AI features remain disabled. Native I/O follows accepted VS Code behavior; guarded store operations remain distinct.
nonFunctional.observability: Log identity/version and operation failures without note text. Surface unsupported syntax and synchronization errors while preserving original content/drafts. Distinguish fake tests from live host evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: sc1's stableId must survive rename/move/archive/restore (s7); the daemon index's reconciliation strategy against the home-dir store's actual file state (so it never serves a stale binding indefinitely) is a design.story decision. Never write/normalize merely by opening a file. Unknown syntax, custom links and diagram fences must round-trip or unsafe edits must be refused with the original preserved. Never silently overwrite newer revisions. Validate cross-window conflict, undo/redo, reload and recovery against normal VS Code behavior.

errors.condition: Background executor fails, times out or cannot reproduce the configured codec; retain draft and refuse application.

preconditions: Install before create, activate after initialization. Initial admission is separate from typing.
Full parser/round-trip/inventory checks must never run in appendTransaction or input dispatch.
postconditions: User doc-changing transactions capture the immutable intent, serialize at most once for immediate bounded recovery staging, and return without grammar validation. Initial/host/selection transactions do not stage or reset the timer.
Each content edit resets a trailing-edge 300 ms timer; no max-wait validation runs during continuous typing. Only one job plus the latest queued generation is retained per executor.

Idle validation is asynchronous and off the input thread. It uses the same factored configured schema/serializer, an intent fingerprint derived from the actual immutable ProseMirror document, and existing independent source-fidelity guards.
A result is usable only for its exact pane session, worker epoch, draft sequence and base version/digest. Superseded results are ignored; the newest draft gets its own idle pass.

Explicit flush cancels the timer and waits for validation plus canonical acknowledgement of the captured generation. Newer typing is retained and does not silently extend or replace that action's capture.
Deactivation cancels timers/jobs and rejects pending flushes without deleting recovery or cancelling already accepted host work.

After the same trailing gap, start configured validation and send one closed validate-draft intent for the already-staged exact generation; explicit captured actions expedite both checks. No validation is performed during continuous normal typing.

The identity-only validate-draft message names paneSessionId,draftSeq,editId,baseVersion,baseDigest; the host resolves the immutable staged bytes rather than trusting a second payload. It confers no apply authority.

returns.meaning: Proposed split between local pending validation, authorization, canonical acknowledgement and true conflict.

errors.condition: Unmatched source/session/base changes or failed current-generation fidelity proof.

preconditions: Staging is distinct from refusal: apply:false must not itself freeze normal typing.
postconditions: Stage immediately increments sequence and posts a recovery-only draft; receipt means recoverable, never validated/applied/saved.
Only successful current-generation admission may authorize the same immutable draft identity for application.
Older acknowledgements update the known base without replacing newer visible text. They never auto-promote an unvalidated latest draft.
A base changed by a confirmed own parent requires fresh admission against the new exact base; unrelated changes freeze and retain the competing draft.
Status distinguishes waiting for typing gap, validating, waiting for host, applied and conflict. Neither receipt nor apply-ack claims disk save.

api.name: ScratchDocumentController
api.signature: class ScratchDocumentController { receive(paneSessionId: string, draft: ScratchDraftProposal): Promise<void>; validate(paneSessionId: string, draftSeq: number, editId: string, baseVersion: number, baseDigest: string): Promise<void>; waitForSequence(paneSessionId: string, draftSeq: number): Promise<ScratchSnapshot>; flush(): Promise<void>; documentChanged(): void; dispose(): Promise<void>; }

returns.meaning: Existing one-per-document native apply lane, with recoverable staging separated from validated application.

errors.condition: Authorization no longer matches the latest accepted draft/base.
Durable staging failed; no receipt or canonical apply is allowed.

preconditions: Retain all URI, session, sequence, duplicate, UTF-8 and encoded-byte checks.
Recovery-only staging performs bounds/identity/storage checks, not full fidelity admission.

A validate intent matches the newest durably staged draft in this live pane, including exact editId/sequence/base; the native source/version/digest still matches. Reject absent, mismatched, superseded, cross-pane or disposed identities.
postconditions: Persist recovery before receipt. Keep received-but-unapplied text through idle waits, worker failure, pane disposal and restart.
Independently verify authorized source/draft in a background host executor, then recheck native version/digest immediately before minimal WorkspaceEdit.

Reuse only fully verified immutable bases keyed by exact source/version/digest and executor/schema epoch. Parse a unique source once per job and share its semantic/inventory products; preserve every existing semantic/raw-syntax/intended-document assertion.
Only one canonical apply runs per document. Already accepted applies may finish; stale validation cannot initiate a new apply.
Clear recovery only after successful acknowledgement delivery to an attached pane; retain unconfirmed data otherwise.
Pending state includes staged drafts awaiting authorization. Deletion cancels on that state rather than waiting indefinitely or authorizing it.

validate is read-only proof preparation, outside the canonical apply lane. Keep at most one active/latest queued host job per document and one prepared exact-generation result; do not block staging behind full verification.

apply:true from the current configured-success generation joins the exact independent host result. If missing, start/join that same bounded read-only check; never bypass it or accept a renderer proof as a host proof. Only both successes plus unchanged native source immediately before WorkspaceEdit permit apply.

A newer stage invalidates any not-yet-accepted older prepared apply/result, including a running result. One native apply already accepted may finish under existing semantics; never overwrite newer renderer text or auto-authorize its descendant.

errors.condition: Explicit action cannot confirm the captured current generation; preserve text and report failure.

postconditions: Save, Send, Undo/Redo and locking explicitly flush the captured generation before their source-dependent action. Send never recaptures a different selection or submits.
Native Save requests a bounded renderer flush; onWillSave remains best effort and can save an earlier canonical version with pending text recoverable, never falsely labelled saved.
Dirty/pending/recovery deletion cancels; clean exact-URI closure/revalidation/unlink, failure reopening and shared independent refresh remain unchanged.
All completed browse/create/error, lock, local asset/CSP, native undo and source-fidelity behaviors remain required; no legacy document channel returns.

api.name: ScratchMarkdownVerifier
api.signature: class ScratchMarkdownVerifier<Document> { invalidate(): void; job(source: string, key: string): { readonly validation: ScratchMarkdownValidationJob<Document>; retainBase(): void }; }

returns.meaning: Preserve current parser/check implementation; add private fully checked candidate adoption machinery without exporting AST or application authority.

errors.condition: Candidate bytes, native canonical version/digest, codec version, executor epoch or current invalidation token do not match.

preconditions: An allowed job completed every existing independent source, candidate, serialization, semantics, raw fingerprints, protected spans, EOL and intent check required by its executor.
The candidate proof is immutable source/inventory only, not parser AST, renderer document or raw allowed boolean.
postconditions: Retain at most one current immutable base proof plus one bounded candidate handoff record associated with the active/latest generation. Canonical confirmation atomically replaces the old base with that exact candidate under the actual observed new version:digest and exact bytes.

Each executor adopts only its own completed fully checked candidate. Adoption is an optimization of source rechecking, never authorization to apply or skip fresh candidate/intent/unchanged-span checks.

Reconcile matching own canonical changes with a successful candidate before unconditional invalidation. Unrelated bytes/version change, missing/timed-out/failed proof, epoch or codec replacement, conflict, reload/disposal invalidates the handoff and falls back to full source verification. A changed version/digest alone cannot transplant a proof; exact canonical bytes and identity confirmation are required.
An invalidation revision blocks active jobs from repopulating a cleared cache; no stale completed result may adopt later.

dataModelChanges.details: Add explicit staged/waiting-idle/validating/authorized/applied/conflict distinctions. Pending admission is not a conflict. Track latest immutable intent and exact base, keep one apply in flight, never auto-authorize newer unvalidated typing.

Existing bounded draft identity is staged with apply:false and later authorized for the same content/sequence. Durable receipt does not authorize native application. Atomically migrate all producer/parser/controller/test consumers; no permissive arbitrary-command fields.

Proposed private immutable job keyed by executor epoch, pane session, draftSeq, base version/digest and configured-codec identity, carrying bounded source references/draft and an actual-document intent fingerprint. Fingerprint semantics match the existing document comparator, including its sole heading-id exception. A parsed copy of the draft cannot serve as its own expected intent. A failed or superseded job never mutates the TextDocument.

New private executor modules are proposed, not current APIs. Keep 1 MiB text and 2 MiB ordinary message limits. Base transfer and candidate jobs use separate bounded messages; do not combine several full snapshots into an oversized message. Worker has no native file/chat/command access. Browser worker is a single local bundled script loaded from trusted fixed code via blob/data-compatible VS Code loading; document content is data only. Retain connect-src 'none', add only the required worker-src policy, terminate/revoke on disposal. Worker codec parity/CSP/native loading are an early qualification gate. Host grammar worker is extension-owned and independently verifies source admission.

Closed identity-only validate-draft intent references one already staged immutable recovery draft. One pane owns many successive generations; document controller owns one active/latest host job and at most one prepared current proof. Configured and host checks run concurrently after the same gap, join by exact pane/epoch/sequence/edit/base identity, and neither receipt nor prepared host proof authorizes native mutation. No persistent DB/entity relationship or sc1 change.

Executor owns one current verified immutable base and at most one fully checked candidate handoff; no AST. Only exact canonical bytes and actual version/digest confirmation in the same codec/epoch adopts the candidate as next base. Replacement is atomic; unrelated change clears it. Worker proof ownership never crosses executors.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Unchanged home scope and validated basename identity; no persisted s7 identity, repo inference, backlinks, ranking, search, attachments or other adjacent-story work.

errorCases.scenario: Validation fails, times out, or worker fails to initialize
errorCases.detection: Executor error/timeout or configured-codec parity check fails.
errorCases.response: Do not authorize; retain durable draft, expose failure and explicit retry/fallback. Dispose failed executor and reject flush waiters.
errorCases.userImpact: Typing remains recoverable; canonical source unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: New typing or source change supersedes a job
errorCases.detection: Result session/epoch/sequence/base version/digest differs from current captured identity.
errorCases.response: Discard result; latest typing receives its own gap validation. Own-parent acknowledgement requires new exact-base admission; unrelated source change freezes with recovery.
errorCases.userImpact: No stale overwrite or automatic promotion.

errorCases.detection: Actual-document intent fingerprint, source syntax inventory or semantic round-trip comparison fails.
errorCases.response: Keep original and draft, show precise refusal; never weaken checks to pass performance.
errorCases.userImpact: Unsafe edit is recoverable rather than applied.

errorCases.detection: Awaited durable write/applyEdit/ack delivery fails or pane detaches.
errorCases.response: No receipt before persistence; retain unconfirmed recovery, finish accepted work once, reject action barrier with actual status.
errorCases.userImpact: No false saved state or duplicate history.

errorCases.detection: Captured-generation barrier times out, refuses or is disposed.
errorCases.response: Pane Save/Send/Undo/Redo/lock reports failure without source-dependent action. Lock blocks input immediately while captured admission completes, commits lock only afterward; failure retains draft and visible state. Native save hook is bounded best effort and must avoid queue reentrancy/deadlock.
errorCases.userImpact: Selection is never replaced with later text; native save may contain earlier canonical source with pending recovery.

errorCases.scenario: Invalid target, size, asset or delete
errorCases.detection: Existing URI/session/bounds/asset checks reject or exact-URI dirty/pending/recovery inspection fails.
errorCases.response: Retain existing guarded refusal, explicit same-file fallback, failed-upload no-reference insertion, clean-close failure reopening and refresh behavior.
errorCases.userImpact: Original, drafts and unrelated tabs remain intact.

errorCases.scenario: Validation intent has no durably staged matching draft
errorCases.detection: Closed identity validation cannot find the same live pane/sequence/edit/base bytes, or persistence is not complete.
errorCases.response: Keep at most one pending latest intent awaiting its matching durable stage; reject mismatch/supersession. Never validate arbitrary unstaged bytes or create native permission.
errorCases.userImpact: Draft remains recoverable; action waits boundedly or reports failure.

errorCases.scenario: One concurrent executor refuses, fails or returns an obsolete identity
errorCases.detection: Exact generation/base/epoch/codec comparison fails or either result is refused/error/timeout.
errorCases.response: Do not apply. Ignore stale outcomes without freezing newer input; a current refusal/failure retains the visible and durable draft and fails captured actions explicitly. Cancel or retire the obsolete peer work without adding an unbounded queue.
errorCases.userImpact: Typing continues; canonical document is not overwritten.

errorCases.scenario: Canonical confirmation does not match a fully checked candidate
errorCases.detection: Exact candidate bytes and accepted generation provenance fail to match the actual observed native source/version/digest, or invalidation revision/worker epoch changed.
errorCases.response: Invalidate candidate/base reuse and run complete source verification. Never infer apply authority from a matching digest or prepared proof alone. Own document-state arriving before apply-ack may hold a bounded untrusted handoff, but may adopt only after exact accepted-identity canonical confirmation; an unrelated change clears it.
errorCases.userImpact: Possible slower next validation, no fidelity loss or unsafe application.

errorCases.scenario: Revised architecture still exceeds original full-bound latency target
errorCases.detection: All ordinary native samples and latest burst/resumed acknowledgements are timed on the original clocks; original150msmedian/1000msp95 gates fail on either required host.
errorCases.response: Keep t15 and BUILD failed, preserve every sample/failure and seek another tracked design decision. Do not reduce bounds, omit slow edits, reinterpret receipt as ack or weaken checks.

edgeCases.input: Continuous typing beyond several timer intervals
edgeCases.expected: No full validation during typing; reset 300ms trailing timer; one active/latest queued bounded job, no repeated snapshots accumulating.

edgeCases.input: Typing resumes while a long validation runs
edgeCases.expected: Rendering remains responsive; result stale and cannot apply; latest generation validates after its own gap.
Capture exact action generation and selection; later typing remains visible/recoverable and cannot silently change the action. Explicit flush bypasses idle delay.
No draft, timer reset, validation or file write.
Disposal cancels timers/jobs/waiters; recovery persists and accepted apply finishes safely. Delete cancels when pending rather than authorizing or hanging.

edgeCases.input: Multiple panes, locked selection, Unicode and CRLF
edgeCases.expected: Preserve existing per-pane selection/lock and host queue, UTF8 bounds, EOL fidelity and click-only bounded composer insertion.

edgeCases.input: Prepared host success arrives before renderer authorization, or authorization arrives before host success
edgeCases.expected: Join only the same current staged generation/base; either arrival alone is read-only. Joining cannot stall durable staging or unrelated panes.

edgeCases.input: Already accepted canonical apply finishes while newer typing is staged
edgeCases.expected: Keep existing accepted-apply semantics; acknowledgement updates base but never replaces newer visible text or authorizes it. Adopt an exact successful accepted candidate only under that canonical identity; freshly validate newer typing against the new base.

edgeCases.input: Newer stage arrives during configured or host work; many panes request verification
edgeCases.expected: No max-wait during continuous typing. Each executor remains one active/latest queued job; global document host queue coalesces fairly without per-pane unbounded workers. Superseded waiters settle explicitly and cannot reopen native apply.

edgeCases.input: Save/Send/Undo/Redo/lock or native autosave captures pending work
edgeCases.expected: Expedite both exact captured checks; all existing current-only action failure, one-second best-effort native Save, lock-confirmation and preference rollback semantics remain. Do not silently recapture later typing.

Native mutation still joins both current successes and exact native guards. Completion remains conditional on unchanged native latency and regression gates.

migrationSteps.action: After fresh human LLD approval, revise PLAN with tracked proof-adoption and concurrent-join tasks plus requalification dependencies; preserve t1-t21 history and failed t15. No implementation starts under the old plan.

Implement and qualify executor-local immutable candidate handoff/adoption with exact canonical confirmation and invalidation. Keep complete source verification as fallback and prove every original fidelity assertion remains.

Implement closed exact-stage validation-intent and concurrent independent host preparation/join without putting staging behind validation or granting apply authority. Update both bridge consumers atomically in the same extension package; qualify races and captured actions.

Requalify packaged CSP/corpus, affected task mappings and floor/current native lifecycle/authoring/interruption; then rerun original full-bound latency. BUILD stays failed on any required skip/missing/failure. Preserve prior measurements.

migration.backwardCompat: sc1 and all daemon/public IPC contracts are unchanged; canonical .md files and apply:false recovery records remain readable. Private bridge/worker protocol changes ship atomically with host and renderer; reject unknown or mismatched protocol/epoch rather than allowing an old pane to bypass checks. Reloading falls back to full verification; no recovery record implicitly resumes or authorizes validation/application.

alternativesConsidered.name: Preserve serial validation and adopt exact verified candidates
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Reuse successful candidate source proofs after canonical confirmation, keeping serial verification.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend existing immutable verifier cache lifetime across an exact own canonical acknowledgement. Reuse only fully checked candidate inventory at matching canonical bytes/version/digest in the same codec epoch; retain independent host checks and the existing serialized configured-then-host contract.
pros: Smallest cache-only correction; no new validation-intent bridge message.
cons: Warm burst evidence already exceeds1s; cache alone is not evidence the original target can hold.
Host admission remains serial on the critical path.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Small cache-only change does not remove serial warm checks.

alternativesConsidered.name: Concurrent independent validation with exact canonical proof adoption
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Start both bounded read-only checks after the gap and join their exact-current results before native application.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reuse the existing pane scheduler, two independent executors, durable staging and canonical controller. Add a closed bounded validation-intent operation for an already staged exact generation; it can compute host proof but never authorizes apply. Only current apply:true authorization plus successful exact-base host proof permits canonical mutation. Each executor may adopt its own fully checked immutable candidate inventory as next-base proof only upon exact canonical bytes/version/digest confirmation; no cross-executor proof, mutable AST, renderer assertion or receipt becomes native authority.
pros: Removes sequential full checks and repeated already-verified base work while retaining all fidelity requirements.
Preserves immediate staging and the existing current-only native apply boundary.
Full native performance remains an objective required gate.
cons: Adds a private validation-intent identity/join and candidate-adoption lifecycle requiring race qualification.
Measured budget is not guaranteed; further profiling may be necessary if the original gate still fails.

alternativesConsidered.name: Concurrent checks without next-base reuse
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Overlap independent passes while invalidating every proof on each canonical revision.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add the same bounded read-only validation-intent/join while retaining unconditional cache invalidation after own canonical changes. Keep all source checks cold for each edit and require both exact successful checks before application.
pros: Simpler proof lifetime than candidate adoption.
cons: Measured configured check alone takes~1.23s before gap/transport; overlap alone cannot plausibly meet1s for ordinary cold checks.
Avoids one bottleneck but retains repeated complete source validation.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cold configured check alone exceeds the target before host latency.
